description: Orca creates and removes every arbor worktree; workers of a task share one Orca Run; a start is idempotent and a failed start is retried on the same Orca Task; the report file decides a dispatch
changelog: Task, partition and integration worktrees are Orca workspaces: the driver creates them with `orca worktree create --repo path:<repo> --name <task> --branch <branch_prefix><task> --base-branch <start> --parent-worktree path:<parent>` and removes them with `orca worktree rm`. Orca chooses the path (task.json `worktree_path` records it), so `worktree.root` in .arbor/config.yaml is gone, as are the `orca worktree set` registration and the need to show external worktrees. A workspace or branch name Orca already holds refuses the start instead of taking a suffixed name. Every worker of a task runs in the task's Orca Run (task.json `orca_run`, created with `orca orchestration run-create`; a session that did not create it takes it over with `run-use`). `worker-start` carries the request's id (`--retry-request`), so `arbor.py run --dispatch d-NNN` on a prepared request never starts a second worker. A start that fails keeps the request prepared: `run` exits 1 with the reason, and the next `run --dispatch` releases the failed Dispatch and retries on the same Orca Task (`--task <id> --retry-of <dispatch>`); the third failed start fails the dispatch. `arbor.py sync` takes the verdict from the report file, whatever `--outcome` the worker sent: a written report is validated as the reply even when the worker settled as failed or ended its turn without `worker_done`. A worker whose turn ended with neither a report nor `worker_done` is reported as idle with the `orca orchestration send` command that asks it to finish; a worker past the executor timeout is failed only when Orca proves it stopped, otherwise it stays pending as `not collected`.
migrationGuide: Before updating, collect every pending worker (`arbor.py sync`) and finish or abandon every started task: a 0.10 worker request has no Run or request id and cannot be started by 0.11, and a 0.10 task worktree was not created by Orca while `arbor.py finish` now removes worktrees through `orca worktree rm` (remove a leftover one with `git worktree remove` and `git branch -D`). Delete `worktree.root` from .arbor/config.yaml (it is ignored). Every repository arbor cuts worktrees from, package repositories of a polyrepo included, must be an Orca project: `orca repo add --path <repo>`; `--external-worktree-visibility show` is no longer needed. With the codex agent, open the repository once in Orca and accept Codex's "Hooks need review" prompt: a worker cannot start while it is pending.
